privacy.pageDescription: How Selftend handles your account, preference, and private CBT record data.
privacy.reviewBanner: This policy requires final legal review before public launch.

sections.title: In short
body: This is the short version, in plain words. The numbered sections below say the same things in full, and they are the ones that count.
Selftend has a minimum age. It is 13 in most countries and higher in some - section 11 lists them.
We ask your date of birth once, to check that age. We never store it. We keep only whether you met the age, the country you chose, and the date we asked.
You do not have to give us an email address. The app works without an account.
What you write in the app is yours. We do not sell it, we do not show you adverts, we do not use it to train AI, and nobody here reads it unless you ask us to or the law requires it.
You can download everything you have written, or delete all of it, from Settings at any time. Deleting is permanent.
If anything here worries you, or you want something removed, write to privacy@selftend.org and a person will answer.

sections.title: 1. Who we are
body: Selftend is a free, open-source cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) programme available on web, iOS, and Android.
Data controller: Selftend (operated by Vasil Yoshev), contact: privacy@selftend.org.
This policy applies to all users of the Selftend application regardless of platform.

sections.title: 2. Data we collect
body: Account data: when you first use the app, a guest account is created for you with no email address or other personal identifier attached - only a random account ID. Your email address and authentication identifiers exist only after you choose to create an account, by registering with an email and password, with Google OAuth, or with Sign in with Apple. If you use Sign in with Apple and choose to hide your email, Apple gives us a private relay address instead of your real one.

Age check data: we ask for your date of birth and your country once, before you start. The date of birth is used for a single comparison and then discarded - it is not sent anywhere, not written to our database, and not kept on your device. What we store is the result: whether you met the minimum age for the country you chose, that country, and the date you were asked.

App data: user preferences (enabled modules, onboarding status, reminder settings) and private CBT thought records or other self-help entries you create. These entries may include wellness or mental-health reflection content if you choose to enter it.

Device data: only when you explicitly enable reminders, we store the technical address needed to deliver them - a push token on native apps, or a browser push subscription (endpoint and keys) on web - along with your time zone and, on web, your browser's user-agent string. We do not perform device fingerprinting and do not collect hardware identifiers, advertising IDs, or your location.

Session and local preference data: an authentication token stored in browser localStorage (web) or Expo SecureStore (mobile) to maintain your signed-in session, plus small local app preferences such as language, theme, and last timer session duration stored on your device.

sections.title: 3. Data we do not collect
body: We do not collect IP addresses for profiling, device fingerprints, location data, contacts, or health data from device APIs. The only photo we store is a profile picture, and only if you choose to upload one; we do not otherwise scan or access your photo library.
We do not store your date of birth, and we do not ask for a document, a photograph, or any other proof of age.
We do not use advertising SDKs, analytics tracking services, behavioral profiling tools, or social media pixels.
We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal data to any third party for any purpose.

sections.title: 4. Legal basis for processing (GDPR Articles 6 and 9)
body: Contract (Art. 6(1)(b)): Processing your email and app data is necessary to provide the service you signed up for - maintaining your account, syncing your records, and delivering the self-help features.
Consent (Art. 6(1)(a)): Notification reminders are only scheduled after you explicitly opt in. You can withdraw consent at any time in Settings.

Explicit consent for sensitive content (GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)): the self-help entries you save can contain wellness, mental-health, or other special-category information. We process that content only with your explicit consent, which you give as a separate, affirmative act - a step of its own, worded on its own, that everyone completes before using the app. It is never bundled into accepting these policies, and it is never inferred from your continued use. If you already have an account, you are shown that step once, the next time this policy changes.

Withdrawing that consent: you can withdraw it at any time by deleting your account in Settings, which removes the entries it covers, or by contacting privacy@selftend.org. Withdrawal does not affect processing that already took place while the consent was in force.

The age check (Art. 6(1)(c) and Art. 9(2)(a)): we ask your age and your country so that we process special-category data only where you can consent to it yourself, and we keep the result as the record that the check happened. Section 11 explains how the minimum age is set.
Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)): Minimal security logging (e.g., authentication events managed by Supabase) to protect the service and users from abuse.

sections.title: 5. How we use your data
body: To authenticate you and maintain your signed-in session across devices.
To store and sync your private thought records and preferences.
To schedule local device reminders or send web push reminders when you opt in.
To process account deletion and data export requests.
We do not use your wellness entries for advertising, training AI models, research, or any purpose beyond delivering the app's features to you.

sections.title: 6. Data processors and sharing
body: Supabase (Supabase Inc., USA): provides authentication, database hosting, and backend infrastructure. Supabase processes your email and app data on our behalf under their Data Processing Agreement. See supabase.com/privacy.
Google (Google LLC, USA): processes your email and account identifiers only if you choose Google OAuth sign-in. See policies.google.com/privacy.

Apple (Apple Inc., USA): processes your authentication request and account identifiers only if you choose Sign in with Apple. If you hide your email, Apple relays messages to you without sharing your address with us. See apple.com/legal/privacy.

Cloudflare (Cloudflare, Inc., USA): serves the static web application via Cloudflare Workers. Cloudflare does not receive or process your personal data beyond standard edge server logs (IP address in access logs, subject to Cloudflare's privacy policy).

Expo (Expo Inc., USA): used for mobile app builds and submission, and for delivering reminder notifications on mobile. When mobile reminders are on, Expo's push service relays your device push token and the generic reminder text; it does not receive your notes, entries, or other content you write in the app.

Sentry (Functional Software, Inc., USA): receives crash reports and error diagnostics - stack traces, app version, device model and OS version, and your pseudonymous account identifier - so we can find and fix defects. Sentry never receives your notes, entries, or anything else you write in the app. See sentry.io/privacy.

Amazon Web Services (Amazon Web Services, Inc., USA): delivers feedback you send through the in-app feedback form to our support mailbox using the Amazon SES email service. That email includes your feedback message and your email address so we can reply to you. See aws.amazon.com/privacy.

Discord (Discord Inc., USA): receives a copy of feedback you send through the in-app feedback form - the feedback category and message text only - posted to a private channel visible only to project maintainers so we can act on feedback quickly. Your email address and account identifiers are never sent to Discord. See discord.com/privacy.
Browser push services (for example Apple, Google, Mozilla, or Microsoft depending on your browser): deliver web push reminders only after you opt in through your browser.
We do not share your data with any third parties other than the processors listed above, and we never share it with advertisers or data brokers.

sections.title: 7. International data transfers
body: Our data processors are based in the United States. For transfers of personal data from the European Economic Area (EEA), United Kingdom, or Switzerland, we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as adopted by the European Commission, or the processor's participation in recognised data transfer frameworks.
You can request a copy of the relevant transfer safeguards by contacting privacy@selftend.org.

sections.title: 8. Data retention
body: Account and app data: retained for as long as your account is active.

Guest accounts: deleted after 12 months of inactivity - twelve months without the app being opened on a device holding the session. The data is removed exactly like self-service deletion: from our live systems immediately, and from backups created beforehand within 90 days.

After account deletion: your personal data (profile, preferences, records) is removed from our live systems immediately. Backups created before deletion are retained for up to 90 days under our backup schedule and then automatically deleted.

Age check: the result - whether you met the minimum age, the country you chose, and the date you were asked - is kept for as long as your account exists and is deleted with it. Your date of birth is never stored, so there is nothing to retain.

Attempts below the minimum age: nothing is retained. The account created for the attempt is deleted immediately, together with anything written during it. Only a local timer stays on the device (see section 12).

Accounts we learn are below the minimum age: if we become aware that an account belongs to someone below the minimum age for their country, we delete the account and its data on becoming aware, without waiting for a request.
Authentication logs: managed and retained by Supabase according to their retention policy.

Feedback messages: feedback you send through the in-app form is delivered to our support mailbox and mirrored (category and message text only) to a private maintainers-only Discord channel. Both copies are kept for as long as needed to act on the feedback. Feedback content is not stored in the app's database.
Local device data (reminder IDs, browser push subscriptions, session tokens): removed when you disable reminders, sign out, delete your account, or delete the app/browser data where applicable.

sections.title: 9. Your rights under GDPR
body: If you are in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, you have the following rights:
Right of access: request a copy of your personal data (available via data export in Settings).
Right to rectification: correct inaccurate data (you can edit your thought records directly in the app).
Right to erasure: delete your account and all associated data (available via self-service deletion in Settings).
Right to data portability: receive your data in a structured, machine-readable JSON format (available via data export in Settings).
Right to restrict processing: request that we limit how we use your data.
Right to object: object to processing based on legitimate interest.
Right to withdraw consent: withdraw consent for reminders at any time in Settings.
Right to lodge a complaint: you may file a complaint with your local data protection supervisory authority.
To exercise any right not available through self-service, contact privacy@selftend.org.

sections.title: 10. Your rights under US state privacy laws
body: If you are a resident of California (CCPA/CPRA), Virginia (VCDPA), Colorado (CPA), Connecticut (CTDPA), or other states with consumer privacy laws:
Right to know: you can request what personal data we collect, use, and disclose.
Right to delete: you can delete your account and all data via self-service in Settings.
Right to opt out of sale: we do not sell your personal data. There is nothing to opt out of.
Right to non-discrimination: we will not treat you differently for exercising your privacy rights.
To exercise any right, use the in-app features or contact privacy@selftend.org.

sections.title: 11. Minimum age
body: Selftend has a minimum age, and it is not the same everywhere. What the app holds - thought records, mood entries, journal text - is special-category data about your health, and the age that matters is the age at which you may consent to that processing yourself. Countries set that age individually, so ours follows theirs.
The minimum age is 13 in Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Malta, Norway, Portugal, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States - and in every other country not named below.
It is 14 in Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Italy, Lithuania and Spain.
It is 15 in Czechia, France, Greece and Slovenia.
It is 16 in Croatia, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania and Slovakia.
It is never below 13, anywhere.

We ask for your date of birth and your country once, before you start, and keep only the result (see section 2). There is no parental-consent route and no identity check: where the law would require one, our minimum age rises instead.

We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone below the minimum age for their country. If we learn that we have, we delete the account and its data promptly. If you believe someone below the minimum age has an account, contact privacy@selftend.org.

sections.title: 12. Cookies and local storage
body: The web version of Selftend uses browser localStorage to store your authentication session token. This is functionally essential and cannot be disabled while using the app.

If the age check is not met, your device stores one further item: a time 24 hours ahead, before which the app will not open again. It holds no personal data, no identifier, and no record of what was answered, and it disappears when you clear the app's or the browser's storage.
We do not use tracking cookies, advertising cookies, or third-party cookies.
If optional analytics are introduced in the future, they will require your explicit consent through the cookie preferences manager before any non-essential storage is used.
You can manage your cookie and storage preferences at any time through the cookie settings available in the app.

sections.title: 13. Security measures
body: All data in transit is encrypted via HTTPS/TLS.

Your entries are encrypted at rest at the field level. The encryption key is held outside the database (in Supabase Vault), so a leaked database dump or backup exposes only ciphertext, not your content.
Database access is protected by Row-Level Security (RLS) - each user can only access their own data.
Mobile session credentials are stored in the device's secure keystore (the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore) via Expo SecureStore.
No service-role keys or database passwords are exposed in the client application.
Supabase infrastructure provides encryption at rest for stored data.

sections.title: 14. Changes to this policy
body: We will update this policy when our practices change. The 'Last updated' date at the top reflects the most recent revision.
If we make material changes, we will notify you through the app (e.g., a consent prompt) before the changes take effect.
Continued use of the app after being notified constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

sections.title: 15. Contact
body: For privacy questions, data requests, or complaints: privacy@selftend.org.
For general support: support@selftend.org.
For security issues: security@selftend.org.

terms.pageDescription: Terms of service for Selftend, a free, private CBT programme.
terms.reviewBanner: These terms require final legal review before public launch.

sections.title: 1. Agreement to terms
body: By creating an account or using Selftend, you agree to these Terms of Service and our Privacy Policy.
If you do not agree, do not create an account or use the app.

sections.title: 2. Eligibility
body: You must be at least 13 years old to use Selftend, or the higher minimum age at which you may consent to the processing of your personal data in your country. Section 11 of the Privacy Policy lists the minimum age country by country.
By using the app, you represent that you meet that age.
If you do not, do not create an account and do not use the app. Accounts we learn are below the minimum age are deleted, together with their data.

sections.title: 3. Product scope and boundaries
body: Selftend is a CBT programme you work through on your own. It is not therapy, medical care, diagnosis, treatment, crisis intervention, or emergency support.
The app provides structured cognitive behavioural exercises for personal reflection. It does not replace professional mental health care.

Do not use this app as your only support in a serious or urgent situation. For medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment, consult a qualified professional. For emergencies, contact local emergency services.

sections.title: 4. User accounts
body: First use of the app creates a guest account for you, with no email or personal identifier attached. Creating a registered account is optional - it keeps the data you already have and lets your records and preferences sync across devices.
If you register, you sign in with your email address and a password, with Google, or with Sign in with Apple. Choose a strong, unique password and keep it confidential.
You are responsible for maintaining access to the email address associated with your account.
One account per person. Do not share account access or create multiple accounts.

sections.title: 5. Acceptable use
body: Use the app for its intended purpose: your own reflection and the CBT programme.
Do not enter personally identifiable information about other people in your thought records without a legitimate reason.
Do not attempt to access other users' data, reverse engineer the service, or exploit vulnerabilities.
Do not use the app to generate content that is illegal, harmful, or violates others' rights.

sections.title: 6. User content and intellectual property
body: Your thought records and personal data belong to you. We claim no ownership of your content.
We do not use your content for advertising, training AI models, research, or any purpose other than providing the service to you.
The Selftend application source code is licensed under AGPL-3.0-only. This license applies to the software, not to your personal data.

sections.title: 7. Data and privacy
body: Our collection and use of your data is governed by our Privacy Policy.
You can export your data in machine-readable format at any time through Settings.
You can permanently delete your account and all associated data through Settings.

sections.title: 8. Free access
body: Selftend is free to use. There are no subscription fees, paywalls, or paid features.
We do not serve advertisements or monetize your data.
Selftend accepts optional donations. They are never required for access to any feature.

sections.title: 9. Availability and changes
body: We aim to keep the service available but do not guarantee uninterrupted access.
We may update, modify, or discontinue features with reasonable notice.
We will notify you of material changes to these terms through the app.

sections.title: 10. Termination
body: You may delete your account at any time through Settings. Deletion is permanent and irreversible.
We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms or are used for abuse.
Upon termination, your data will be deleted in accordance with our Privacy Policy's retention schedule.

sections.title: 11. Disclaimers
body: The app is provided "as is" and "as available" without warranties of any kind, whether express or implied.
We do not warrant that the app will meet your requirements, be error-free, or be available without interruption.
We do not provide medical, psychological, or professional advice. Content in the app is for informational and self-help purposes only.
Your use of the app and reliance on any content is at your sole risk.

sections.title: 12. Limitation of liability
body: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, Selftend and its maintainers shall not be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages arising from your use of the app.
This includes, without limitation, damages for loss of data, goodwill, or other intangible losses.
Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud, or any other liability that cannot be excluded by law.

sections.title: 13. Changes to these terms
body: We may update these terms from time to time. The 'Last updated' date reflects the most recent revision.
If we make material changes, we will notify you through the app before the changes take effect.
Continued use of the app after notification constitutes acceptance of the revised terms. If you do not agree, delete your account.

sections.title: 14. Contact
body: For questions about these terms: support@selftend.org.
For privacy matters: privacy@selftend.org.
For security issues: security@selftend.org.

crisis.pageDescription: This app is not emergency support and is not monitored. If you are in danger, contact local emergency services.

sections.title: Immediate danger
body: If you might hurt yourself or someone else, or if anyone is in immediate danger, contact local emergency services now.
This app is not monitored by crisis responders and cannot provide emergency help.

sections.title: Finding crisis support
body: Crisis services vary by country. Find A Helpline (https://findahelpline.com) maintains a reviewed directory of crisis and emotional-support services by country.
If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number instead of searching the directory.

sections.title: How this app should be used
body: The app can help with structured reflection when there is time and safety to reflect.
It should not delay contacting emergency services, a crisis line, a trusted person nearby, or a qualified professional when urgent support is needed.

accountDeletion.pageDescription: How to permanently delete your Selftend account and all associated data.

sections.title: What deletion does
body: Deleting your account permanently removes all data associated with it: your profile, preferences, all thought records (including archived ones), and authentication credentials.
Deletion is irreversible. Once completed, your data cannot be recovered.
Your data is removed from our live systems immediately. Backups created before deletion are automatically deleted within 90 days.

sections.title: How to delete your account
body: Self-service (recommended): Go to Settings → Account → Delete my account. You will be asked to confirm before deletion proceeds.

Email request (fallback): Send a deletion request to privacy@selftend.org from the email address associated with your account. Include your account email and ask for complete account and data deletion.

sections.title: What to know
body: Before deleting, you may want to export your data using the Export feature in Settings.
After deletion, you can create a new account with the same email address, but none of your previous data will be available.
If you only want to stop using the app temporarily, you can simply close it - or, on a registered account, sign out - instead of deleting your account.

cookies.pageDescription: How the web version of Selftend uses browser storage.

sections.title: What are cookies and local storage
body: Cookies are small text files placed on your device by websites. Local storage (localStorage) is a browser feature that allows websites to store data locally on your device.
Selftend primarily uses browser localStorage rather than traditional cookies.

sections.title: Essential storage (required)
body: We use browser localStorage to store your authentication session token. This is strictly necessary for the app to function - it keeps you signed in between visits.
This storage cannot be disabled while using the app. If you clear your browser storage, you will need to sign in again.
The app also stores small local preferences, such as language, theme, and last timer session duration. These preferences stay on your device and are not used for tracking.

If the age check is not met, one further item is stored on the device: a time 24 hours ahead, before which the app will not open again. It holds no personal data and no identifier, and clearing the app's or the browser's storage removes it.

sections.title: Optional cookies (consent required)
body: Selftend does not currently use any optional or analytics cookies.
If optional analytics or functionality cookies are introduced in the future, they will not be set until you provide explicit consent through the cookie preferences manager.
You will always be able to use the app fully without accepting optional cookies.

sections.title: Third-party cookies
body: Selftend does not set or use any third-party cookies.
We do not use advertising networks, social media widgets, or third-party tracking pixels that would set cookies on your device.

sections.title: Managing your preferences
body: You can manage your cookie and storage preferences at any time through the cookie settings available in the app footer (web) or in Settings.
You can also clear all website data through your browser settings, which will remove the session token and sign you out.
For questions about our use of cookies and storage, contact privacy@selftend.org.

sections.title: Is Selftend therapy?
body: No. Selftend is a CBT programme you work through on your own, with no practitioner involved. It is not therapy, counseling, diagnosis, treatment, or a substitute for a licensed mental health professional. If you need clinical care, contact a qualified provider in your area.

sections.title: Can it help in a crisis?
body: No. Selftend cannot help in an emergency. If you are in crisis or at risk of harm, contact local emergency services or a crisis line. The in-app crisis page lists resources we currently know about.

sections.title: Is it really free? What's the catch?
body: It is free. No ads, no in-app purchases, no subscription paywalls for care. Selftend is operated as a non-profit project. It accepts optional donations toward its running costs; they never restrict access to the app.

sections.title: Do I need an account?
body: No. First use creates a guest account automatically, with no email or personal identifier attached, and the whole app works without registering. Creating an account is optional: it keeps the data you already have, lets records sync across devices, and protects them if this device is lost or cleared. Guest accounts inactive for 12 months are deleted. Local-only and bring-your-own-Supabase modes are on the post-MVP roadmap.

sections.title: What data does Selftend collect?
body: An email only if you register, preferences, and the records you choose to create - plus a push token only if you turn on reminders. Your date of birth is asked once for the age check and never stored; we keep the result and the country you chose. No device fingerprints or hardware identifiers, no advertising or analytics SDKs. Full details in the privacy policy.

sections.title: Who can see my records?
body: Your records are private to your account. Records are scoped to your account through Supabase Row-Level Security and HTTPS in transit. We do not read your records except to fulfil a verified privacy request, investigate a security incident, or satisfy a legal obligation.

sections.title: Can I export or delete my data?
body: Yes. Settings has a one-tap JSON export and a self-service account deletion. Deleted accounts are removed from our live systems immediately; backups created beforehand are automatically deleted within 90 days.

sections.title: Why is there no AI counselor?
body: Because we don't think a self-help app should pretend to be one. Selftend has no AI therapist, AI counselor, or AI coach, and nothing you write is used to train AI models.

sections.title: What is the minimum age?
body: 13 in most countries, and 14, 15 or 16 in some - the privacy policy lists them. The number is not our view of who benefits from CBT. It is the age at which the law where you live lets you agree, by yourself, to an app holding reflections about your own mental health, and where that age is higher, ours is too. We ask for your date of birth and your country once, at the start, and keep only whether you met it.

sections.title: For parents and guardians
body: Selftend is a free, non-profit CBT app that a person works through on their own: thought records, mood and habit tracking, breathing, grounding, gratitude, meditation and short lessons. There is no therapist, no counsellor, and no AI pretending to be either. It is not treatment and it is not crisis support - the app says so, and its crisis page points to local emergency services.

There is a minimum age, asked before anyone starts: 13 in most countries and higher in several, following the age at which a person may consent to this kind of data processing where they live. The privacy policy lists it country by country.

On data: no adverts, no advertising or analytics SDKs, no profiling, and nothing sold or shared for marketing. Entries are private to the account, encrypted, and reachable only through it. Registering is optional - the app works without an email address - and everything can be exported or permanently deleted from Settings at any time.

On design: reminders are off until someone turns them on, and go off again in one tap. Nothing counts days, ranks anyone, or measures how often the app is opened, and skipping a day changes nothing in the app.

If you believe someone below the minimum age for their country is using Selftend, write to privacy@selftend.org with what you can tell us; we delete the account and its data on becoming aware. You can also ask us to delete an account belonging to a child you are responsible for.
For anything else, support@selftend.org reaches us.

sections.title: Are reminders annoying?
body: They are off by default. If you turn them on in Settings, you can pick a time, change it whenever you like, and turn them off anytime.

sections.title: Can I use Selftend too much?
body: Not by count. No number of records is watched, and none is judged: Selftend does not read your records back to you. What matters is how a tool is being used, not how often. A thought record helps when it moves from "why am I like this" toward "what is the evidence"; it has stopped helping when you re-open the same thought to feel certain, or when challenging has become checking. Either of those, or reflection that consistently leaves you worse, is a pattern worth bringing to a professional. The programme's own rhythm - check-ins, a record when a feeling shifts, a weekly review - is the pace.

sections.title: Is Selftend open source?
body: Yes - the code is licensed under AGPL-3.0. Issues, contributor docs, and the roadmap are public on GitHub. The Selftend name, logo, and branding are not licensed for reuse.

sections.title: How can I contact you, and what should I expect?
body: Use support@selftend.org for product questions and bug reports, privacy@selftend.org for data requests, and security@selftend.org for security concerns.

Include the minimum needed to help: platform, browser or app version, steps to reproduce, expected and actual behaviour. Please do not include the body of your thought records or other sensitive self-help content in email.
We acknowledge support emails within a week during launch and complete valid GDPR/CCPA privacy requests within one month of receipt.
